tier_reason: Downgraded C to D: the charted 3x over malloc comes from a harness in which malloc pays heap growth and page faults for about 4 GB of live blocks while the linear and stack allocators never touch memory and the pool's page faults fell outside the timed region (Blosc and AssemblyScript precedent), and the measured allocators carry correctness bugs (pool double hand-out after Reset, free-list corruption).

corrections.caveats: First-party charts (malloc about 1500 ms vs free list about 360 ms) that cannot be reproduced: the harness is hard-coded to 10 operations, the pool sizes in main.cpp are too small for 1M operations, the default build is unoptimized and the free list is timed only with LIFO frees. The charted test allocates all N blocks (about 4 GB at 1M) before freeing, so malloc pays heap growth and page faults while the linear and stack allocators never touch memory and the old pool Init took its page faults outside the timed region; the 3x gap is likely mostly page faults. Correctness: PoolAllocator::Reset keeps the free list but zeroes the offset (one chunk can go out twice), Init leaks the old buffer, FreeList FindBest returns a wrong previousNode, remainders smaller than the 16-byte header overflow into the next block (issue #4), Free is wrong with nonzero alignment padding (#18), Stack Free ignores ptr. The charts predate the 2024-2026 fixes.
